title: Revoked API key reintroduced after deployment rollback, causing temporary privilege resurfacing
creator: Priya Natarajan
description: Customer-reported incidents across Dedicated and Private deployments: several customers observed that API keys previously revoked were briefly accepted again following a control-plane deployment rollback. Impact window ~5-20 minutes depending on region and edge cache TTL. This is a high-severity auth bypass affecting token/API-key revocation guarantees. Affected surfaces: API key auth in gateway, session reconciliation on dedicated pools, and private control planes with local cache replicas.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Revoke an API key via control plane. 2) Confirm revocation shows in primary DB and propagated cache invalidation webhook is enqueued. 3) Deploy control-plane update that includes a DB migration and config change. 4) Intentional failed deploy / rollback is triggered (simulated). 5) Observe that old config artifact (pre-revocation mapping) is re-applied to some edge nodes; clients with revoked key can still authenticate for short window on those nodes.
mitigation:
- Emergency: Manually blacklisted affected API key IDs in gateway enforcement layer (blacklist pushed to all regions).
- Invalidated Redis replication caches and forced TTL=0 eviction on edge nodes.
- Temporarily raised auth cache TTL propagation to immediate revalidate for control-plane-change events.
- Customer comms: sent incident notes to impacted accounts and offered scoped post-mortem.
- Reverted rollback sequence on staging to reproduce and confirm mitigation removes acceptance of revoked keys.
root_cause: A combination of (1) deployment rollback re-applying an older service configuration bundle that still referenced stale API-key mapping artifacts, and (2) asynchronous cache invalidation (webhook -> queue -> edge workers) that did not treat rollback as a config-change trigger for forced revalidation. The older bundle also restored a short-lived in-memory map used for fast lookup, which overwrote the blacklist in some nodes during restart ordering.
proposed_fix: 1) Treat deployment rollbacks as a config-change event that triggers full cache invalidation and immediate revalidation of auth artifacts. 2) Remove single-source-of-truth ambiguity: persist authoritative revocation state in primary DB and implement deterministic reconcile on boot before accepting requests. 3) Add a short-lived "revoke_epoch" header in control-plane bundles so nodes ignore older bundles when reconciling. 4) Add an emergency blacklisting API which bypasses local in-memory maps and consults the authoritative revocation store for critical keys.
rollout_plan:
- Patch candidate built on branch fix/auth-rollback-invalidate (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/1523).
- Internal canary in us-west for 2 hours, monitor auth-accept rate for revoked keys.
- If stable, expand to multi-region over 6 hours with rolling restarts ensuring reconcile completes before traffic.
- Post-deploy: run replay tests from incident logs to confirm no acceptance of revoked keys.
- Post-mortem scheduled and follow-up tasks assigned to infra and runtime teams.
